## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage
data.title: Spike: prove the shared campaign core runs headless (wave sequencer + upgrade choices)

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want an executable contract (failing tests) for the two level-scaling axes before any production code exists, so the curves, rounding rules and cap behaviour are pinned before implementation.

This is the test-first item for the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` module and the `GameRules` scaling data (AC "Data-driven level-scaling curves" and the unit-test part of AC "Tests" of the parent item AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Create `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new file) and extend `src/core/rules.test.ts` with tests that pin the agreed contract. These tests must **fail on pre-change HEAD** because neither the module nor the rules fields exist yet.

Curve contract to pin:

- `enemyCountMultiplier(level)`: `1.0` at level 1, `2.0` at level 10, linear in between (assert the exact formula value at level 5, e.g. `1 + (level - 1) * (1.0 / 9)`), monotonically non-decreasing across 1–10.
- `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)`: `0.18` at level 1 (equal to the exported `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`), `0.05` at level 10, monotonically non-increasing across 1–10, and `chance(10) <= 0.3 * chance(1)`.
- Extra Life proportionality: the small-asteroid Extra Life chance scales by the same ratio as the per-kill chance (`chance(level) / chance(1)`), so level 1 equals `rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` exactly.
- Input clamping: levels below 1 clamp to 1, levels above the campaign maximum clamp to the maximum, and non-finite/non-integer inputs resolve to a documented clamped integer (no `NaN` output).
- Count application helper (`applyEnemyCountScaling` or the agreed equivalent): documented round-half-up rule, floor of 1, per-group safety cap of 200, `single`-formation groups left at exactly 1, and a level-1 identity transform (deep-equal input/output).
- Rules: the new scaling fields have documented defaults (1.0→2.0 multiplier, 0.18→0.05 drop chance), are clamped on load, and a legacy persisted blob without them loads with the defaults merged (backwards-compatible, no schema break).

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests exist and fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (module/rules fields absent); record the failure output in a comment on this item.
- Tests cover monotonicity, clamping, level-1 identity, rounding rule, `single` groups, the 200 cap, Extra Life proportionality and legacy rules-blob merging.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).
- Every test name states the behaviour it pins; no asserts without a stated reason.

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Tests** — Unit tests cover curve monotonicity/clamping, count application (rounding, `single` groups, caps, L1 identity, seeded determinism), per-level drop chance, Extra Life proportionality and game↔gym parity. New tests fail on the pre-change code and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the level-scaling implementation item.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want one pure, data-driven source of truth for the campaign's enemy-count multiplier and per-kill power-up drop chance, so both the game and the gyms tune from the same values.

Implements the first two "Desired change" steps of AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P and satisfies its "Data-driven level-scaling curves" AC.

## What to do

- Add `src/core/levelScaling.ts` — Phaser-free, pure and side-effect free. Exports `enemyCountMultiplier(level)`, `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)`, the Extra Life ratio helper, the count-application helper used by the campaign build seam, and the documented default constants.
- Extend `GameRules` in `src/core/rules.ts` with the tunable scaling data (level-1 base chance, level-10 endpoint, campaign level span, count cap), with defaults, validation/clamping and backwards-compatible loading of existing persisted blobs.
- Keep `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` as the documented **level-1 base value** so existing imports keep their meaning; derive higher levels from it.
- Document the formulas, the rounding rule, the floor and the cap in JSDoc (this is the single place a tuner changes the curves).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/core/levelScaling.ts` has no Phaser dependency, is importable under Node/vitest, and is pure (same inputs ⇒ same outputs, no I/O).
- Defaults produce a linear `1.00 → 2.00` enemy-count multiplier across levels 1–10 and a `0.18 → 0.05` per-kill drop chance that is monotonically non-increasing; Extra Life follows the same ratio.
- `loadRules()` merges the new fields into legacy blobs, clamps out-of-range values and never throws; existing rules tests keep passing.
- Level 1 resolves to exactly today's behaviour (0.18 per-kill chance, unchanged Extra Life default).
- The test-first item's contract tests pass.
- Tuning values are documented in code comments with the rationale (mid/late campaign over-supply).

- Parent AC traceability (verbatim from AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): **Data-driven level-scaling curves** — A pure, Phaser-free shared module (proposed `src/core/levelScaling.ts`) exposes `enemyCountMultiplier(level)` and `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` backed by tunable defaults (proposed: extend `GameRules`), with inputs clamped to the campaign range. Defaults: enemy-count multiplier **1.00 at L1 → 2.00 at L10** (linear across 1–10); per-kill power-up drop chance **0.18 at L1 → 0.05 at L10** (monotonically non-increasing); the small-asteroid Extra Life chance scales by the same ratio. Level 1 values reproduce today's behaviour exactly.

## Key Files

- `src/core/levelScaling.ts` (new)
- `src/core/rules.ts`
- `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts`, `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Write level-scaling curve and rules contract tests" (test-first). Blocks the campaign-count, drop-chance, gym and harness items.
